normative_action: The code-reviewer subagent performs an independent read-only review: Write, Edit, MultiEdit and NotebookEdit are disallowed; it must not edit, create or delete files or run commands that change the repository.
exceptions: Bash is not tool-disallowed; the no-change duty for shell use is instruction-only.

normative_action: code-review is the canonical procedure: the reviewer reads .claude/skills/code-review/SKILL.md if not already loaded, follows it from scope to output, does not redefine review criteria, and returns findings in the code-review output format.

Dependency addition/update commands (npm/pnpm/yarn install|add naming a package, update/upgrade/dedupe, npm audit fix, ng add, ng update <pkg>, dotnet add package, dotnet package add|update, nuget install|update, Install-Package/Update-Package, and restores carrying a force flag) are denied until the add-dependency workflow has been completed; the command is then re-run with the trailing comment `# add-dependency: reviewed`.
trigger_scope: Bash/PowerShell commands incl. bash -c / cmd /c / pwsh -Command wrappers
exceptions: The marker comment is self-certified by the agent; bare restores from the lockfile (npm ci, yarn) pass.

normative_action: Dependency-removal commands (npm uninstall|remove|rm|r|un|unlink, pnpm/yarn remove, dotnet remove package, dotnet package remove, Uninstall-Package) are likewise denied until the add-dependency workflow has been completed and the command carries `# add-dependency: reviewed`; a removed package manifest is reported for confirmation that the removal was intended and approved.
modality: MUST (PreToolUse deny; PostToolUse confirmation message on removed manifests)
why_extra_or_uncertain: The oracle's dependency policies (DEP-001..DEP-005) govern additions and updates; no oracle policy subjects dependency removal to a review workflow or approval confirmation.

normative_action: A dependency command using --force or --legacy-peer-deps (npm -f included) receives the instruction to resolve the actual peer-dependency conflict instead.
exceptions: The force message is attached only while the review marker is absent; with `# add-dependency: reviewed` a forced command is not denied by the hook.

normative_action: Changing the project reference graph (dotnet add|remove reference, dotnet reference add|remove, or a .csproj ProjectReference change) is Reserved unless an accepted decision already requires the reference, even when the new reference would be legal: commands are denied unless they carry `# project-references: approved` after the Decision Request; post-change findings ask to confirm the change was approved and recorded, or revert it.
exceptions: Reference already required by an accepted decision; marker comment after approval.
why_extra_or_uncertain: ARC-001 already permits inward references and ARC-020 gates consequential changes such as new projects/layers; no oracle policy makes every legal reference edge a Reserved decision.

normative_action: Repository-changing Git commands (every subcommand not in the read-only list or read-only argument forms, e.g. commit, push, merge, rebase, reset, add, fetch, pull, checkout <target>, stash push, branch/tag changes, config writes) trigger a permission prompt stating they may run only when the user explicitly requested them; procedure git-workflow.
exceptions: Read-only forms (status, diff, log, branch --list, stash list, ...) pass.

normative_action: When instruction files change (CLAUDE.md, the decision register, .claude/** except .hook-state and settings.local.json), check-instructions runs and its errors are fed back to the agent.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Structural self-validation of the instruction system; not derived from any V2 policy.

normative_action: A CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md change triggers the instruction to run the custom-settings workflow to synchronize every affected surface, and at Stop a reminder to confirm the synchronization.
exceptions: Stop reminder once per exact state; Git work trees only.

normative_action: A SPECIFICATION.md change triggers the instruction to confirm it stays consistent with CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md and records only approved behavior.
Removing a project file is reported as a project-graph change to confirm as intended and approved (CLAUDE.md Decisions; project-structure).
A moved manifest/project is reported so that every reference to it is updated (project-structure).

When Domain .cs files or Infrastructure/Persistence Configurations/AppDbContext change without any Seeding/DbSeeder change (and a DbSeeder.cs exists), the agent is stopped once to confirm seeded entities are unaffected or update the development seeder.
modality: SHOULD (Stop: decision block once per exact state)
trigger_scope: Stop in a Git work tree
exceptions: Only when a DbSeeder.cs exists under backend/; once per exact state.

normative_action: When migration files (excluding .Designer.cs and ModelSnapshot.cs) are added or changed, the agent is stopped once to review them before committing.
modality: SHOULD (Stop: decision block once per exact state)
trigger_scope: Stop in a Git work tree

normative_action: When production code (backend .cs or frontend .ts, excluding tests, .spec.ts and migrations) changed without any test change, the agent is stopped once to confirm existing coverage or add tests.
modality: SHOULD (Stop: decision block once per exact state)
trigger_scope: Stop in a Git work tree
exceptions: once per exact state; outside Git the Stop check fails visibly (exit 1) instead.

normative_action: Instruction artifacts are organized by two questions: the Kind (OP, DEC, STD, KNW, WF, ENF, IN) decides mechanism, location and loading; the Scope (common, backend, backend-tests, frontend, delivery, repo/meta) decides the directory and path globs (standard globs start in the scope's territory; repo/meta has no standards; a delivery standard is created only when a path-triggered rule is needed).
why_extra_or_uncertain: Instruction-system classification scheme of the K design; not derived from any V2 policy.

normative_action: Conformance dependencies point WF -> KNW -> STD -> DEC -> OP and ENF -> STD/DEC (declared in the header and Conforms to: lines); routing pointers (See also/Workflow/Technique/Procedure/Enforced by, workflow invocations, CLAUDE.md routing table, register Details in/Affects) may point anywhere; every other reference is a conformance dependency checked for direction and acyclicity; skill references/ files are read only by their skill; standards cite decision IDs instead of restating decisions, and decision summaries exist only in the register.
exceptions: Routing pointers are exempt from the direction rule.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Internal reference discipline of the instruction system; no oracle policy governs how instruction files reference each other or where decision summaries may appear.

normative_action: The maintainer map lists every artifact with its owner, loading, enforcement and 'Extend here' routing; the Decision -> Affects view is generated from the register and must match it (verified by check-instructions).
why_extra_or_uncertain: Template maintenance rule (single owner per topic, map synchronized with the register); not a V2 policy.

normative_action: Domain stays independent of mapping-library concerns (in addition to EF Core, ASP.NET Core, HTTP, persistence and external-service concerns).
why_extra_or_uncertain: ARC-002 lists EF Core, ASP.NET Core, HTTP, persistence and external-service implementation concerns; mapping-library independence of Domain is an additional restriction (DEP-011 only governs when Mapster is approved).

normative_action: Backend C# style rules: prefer primary constructors for simple DI/initialization (regular constructors when validation is non-trivial or the codebase uses them) and records where value semantics are intended (not every DTO/Domain type); keep implementation details non-public unless part of the public API and use sealed for design intent, not as speculative optimization; prefer var when the type is obvious; use standard .NET naming (PascalCase types/members, camelCase parameters/locals, meaningful names; private fields per repository convention).
exceptions: Repository conventions for private-field naming; established codebase style for constructors.
why_extra_or_uncertain: RUN-009 delegates conventions to the repository and .editorconfig and RUN-024 covers only namespaces, one type per file and Async naming; the oracle classifies constructor/record/visibility/type-inference preferences as non-oracle style (EXC-003). The naming and var parts mirror .editorconfig (a RUN-009 convention source), but the visibility, sealed, record and primary-constructor preferences have no .editorconfig or oracle counterpart, so the loaded standard adds style constraints the 196 do not contain.

normative_action: 'Commit package.json and package-lock.json, and keep the lockfile consistent with every dependency change.'
why_extra_or_uncertain: Open question: read literally, the standard instructs a git commit of the manifests, which GOV-015 permits only on explicit request; read as 'keep them under version control', it restates DEP-007. The imperative wording does not settle which.

normative_action: HTTP status codes and transport response semantics belong to the API layer; Application and Domain must not return IActionResult, ProblemDetails or ASP.NET Core status codes.
ProblemDetails for non-validation HTTP failures and ValidationProblemDetails for request validation; keep machine-readable error contracts stable and safe.
Choose 200/201/202/204 by actual HTTP semantics (not 200 for everything, 201 merely for an internal insert, 202 for completed work); keep status behavior consistent across similar endpoints.
A successful collection query with zero matches returns 200 with an empty collection, not 404.
401 for missing/failed authentication, 403 for an authenticated principal not permitted; 404 to hide a protected resource must be a deliberate, consistent security policy.
409 for a valid request conflicting with current state; 412 when an explicit HTTP precondition such as If-Match fails.
Do not introduce API versioning merely because an API exists; add it only for published compatibility or coexisting client generations.

Once relied on by external clients, an API version must not change incompatibly without compatibility treatment: a breaking change requires a new version or another explicitly approved compatibility strategy.
When explicit versioning is required, use one strategy consistently — URL-segment versioning unless requirements justify another.
Do not create separate Domain or persistence models merely because the API has multiple versions; isolate version-specific transport contracts at the API boundary when practical.
Swagger/OpenAPI metadata describes the API that actually runs (routes, important statuses, schemas, authentication behavior) and does not document speculative responses.
Swagger UI is enabled in Development and exposed elsewhere only when deployment requirements explicitly justify it.

Dependencies point inward: Domain references no other application project; Application references Domain; Infrastructure references Application and Domain; Api references Application and may reference Infrastructure only for composition and DI registration.

Inner layers never depend on outer layers and Domain/Application do not reference Infrastructure-specific types; when a feature seems to need Domain -> Application, Domain -> Infrastructure or Application -> Infrastructure, reconsider the abstraction boundary instead.
Domain stays independent of EF Core, ASP.NET Core, HTTP, persistence and external-service implementation concerns.

Simple domain entities; CRUD-oriented and straightforward workflow rules belong in Application Services; validation rules, immutable fields, status transitions or allowed/forbidden edits do not by themselves justify a Rich Domain Model.

Move behavior into Domain only when non-trivial invariants or behavior materially benefit from domain-level encapsulation; otherwise a Rich Domain Model or DDD tactical pattern requires approval (Reserved).
exceptions: unless the approved specification already requires that design

normative_action: Do not add factory methods, private setters, transition methods, Aggregate Roots, Domain Events, Specifications, Domain Services, systematic Value Objects or similar constructs merely to appear domain-driven.
Application Services orchestrate use cases; a large service is a signal to reconsider responsibilities, not a reason for another architectural pattern.
Define persistence and external-service abstractions in Application when use cases require them; keep infrastructure details out of Application.
Application must not use DbContext, DbSet<T>, EF Core APIs, provider-specific types or ASP.NET Core transport types.
Controllers stay thin: bind and validate HTTP input, invoke Application services, translate outcomes to HTTP responses.
Controllers do not contain business logic, access DbContext or concrete repositories, or construct infrastructure services manually.
Program.cs is the composition root and may register Infrastructure implementations; Controllers still do not consume Infrastructure implementation types.
Do not duplicate equivalent DTOs across API and Application merely to create layer-shaped types; introduce transport-specific contracts when separation gives a concrete boundary benefit.
Specific repository interfaces represent actual cohesive Application persistence needs, not table-mirroring generic CRUD contracts; defined in Application and implemented in Infrastructure.
exceptions: In an explicitly approved DDD design Aggregate Roots are natural repository boundaries.

normative_action: Repository interfaces do not expose IQueryable<T>, DbSet<T>, DbContext, EF Core expressions or provider types; LINQ-to-EF stays in Infrastructure; return materialized entities, collections, projections or explicit result models.

Application does not depend on IGenericRepository<T> or another generic CRUD contract; a generic repository/base class may exist only as an Infrastructure detail removing real duplication, not replacing EF Core query capabilities.

IUnitOfWork is the commit boundary: repositories stage changes and do not call SaveChangesAsync independently; Application Services decide when to commit; Infrastructure implements IUnitOfWork over the DbContext.

Repositories in one use case share the same scoped Unit of Work and DbContext; repositories are injected explicitly; IUnitOfWork is not a repository container or service locator exposing repositories as properties.
No explicit transaction APIs until a concrete use case needs control beyond a normal SaveChangesAsync.

EF Core is an Infrastructure implementation detail: use it fully inside Infrastructure, never leak its concepts into Application, and do not cripple repository implementations to preserve a generic abstraction.
Constructor injection for required dependencies; avoid service-locator and property-injection patterns.
Service lifetimes must be valid; never capture a shorter-lived dependency inside a longer-lived service.
Registration stays with the owning layer: Application registers Application services, Infrastructure registers persistence and adapters, Api remains the composition root.
Distributed caching is Reserved.

Caching is an optimization, not an architecture requirement: introduce it only for a clear measured or reasoned need and choose the implementation by deployment, consistency and staleness requirements, never merely because a value is read often.
Cache technology stays out of Domain; infrastructure cache APIs do not leak into Application without a deliberate boundary abstraction.

Cache keys uniquely represent the cached value with every relevant dimension (identifier, tenant, user when user-specific, locale, query parameters); avoid global keys for user- or tenant-specific data.
Every cache entry has a lifetime or another explicit invalidation strategy.
Invalidate or update cache entries consistently with successful underlying mutations; the cache never becomes a second source of truth.

Follow the repository's conventions and .editorconfig; use modern C# when it improves clarity but do not mechanically modernize working code (including no mechanical constructor conversion); consistency and readability matter more than language features.
No style-only rewrites outside the requested change unless explicitly asked; avoid mixing large formatting or modernization changes with functional work.

New code: file-scoped namespaces when consistent; one primary top-level type per file named after it (small private/nested types may stay); Async suffix unless an existing/framework contract makes it inappropriate; do not reorganize an existing file merely for preferred member ordering.
Use async APIs for asynchronous I/O and never block them with .Result, .Wait() or similar sync-over-async patterns.
Propagate CancellationToken through asynchronous operations when cancellation is meaningful; no cancellation parameters on purely synchronous code without a use case.
Use TimeProvider for logic whose behavior depends on the current clock and needs deterministic tests; stored timestamps and explicit dates are not clock dependencies; no mechanical replacement.
Clear, correct code first; no specialized optimizations without a concrete reason; prefer measurement/profiling evidence for non-trivial optimization.
Compiled queries, ValueTask<T>, ArrayPool/MemoryPool and manual pooling, custom serialization, aggressive caching and raw SQL for performance only for a measured or clearly demonstrated need.

Unexpected failures propagate to centralized IExceptionHandler handling without repetitive catch/log/rethrow; catch only where the layer can recover, translate into its own outcome, apply a defined fallback, add context preserving the original, or perform required cleanup.
Public API errors do not expose stack traces, SQL, connection strings, internal paths, secret values or sensitive exception details.
Unexpected exceptions are logged once, by default at the handling boundary, not repeatedly across repository, Application, Controller and global handler.
Represent common expected outcomes explicitly when useful (null, bool, typed outcome) without forcing a generic Result<T> and without HTTP-named outcome categories in Application.
A project-wide Result model is Reserved.
Do not establish business exceptions as the default architecture or throw/catch exceptions merely to jump between normal branches.

Use FluentValidation for explicit request/use-case validation where appropriate and keep each concern at its owning boundary (API transport, Application use-case/workflow rules, Domain invariants, Infrastructure external assumptions); do not move Domain invariants into FluentValidation merely because it is available or duplicate rules mechanically.
Normal client-request cancellation is not a server failure: do not map it to a generic 500 or log it as an unhandled error.

Strongly typed options validated at startup when missing/invalid values prevent correct or secure operation; no scattered string-based IConfiguration lookups (direct access belongs in composition root, provider setup and infrastructure registration).
ILogger<T> with structured message templates and stable property names; avoid interpolation that makes structured values opaque.
When Serilog is configured use DI-integrated AddSerilog with environment-aware configuration; application code depends on ILogger<T>.
Health checks stay cheap and deterministic, not business workflows or expensive/mutating database work.

Liveness does not depend on external dependencies whose unavailability would cause restart loops (by default no database or remote API checks); readiness may depend on capabilities required to serve traffic and reflects startup completion and required-dependency availability.
Publicly reachable health responses do not expose secrets, credentials, connection details, stack traces or unnecessary diagnostics.

Production containers use an appropriate runtime image (the ASP.NET Core runtime image for APIs) rather than the SDK image for convenience and avoid switching to root merely to bypass filesystem problems.
Never create and dispose a new HttpClient per request; use IHttpClientFactory or another long-lived strategy.
Infrastructure translates remote HTTP responses into Application-facing abstractions; HttpResponseMessage and transport concerns do not leak into Application.
External I/O calls have a bounded execution time appropriate to the operation; avoid overlapping timeout mechanisms with unclear combined behavior.
Retry only when repeating is safe; never automatically retry state-changing operations without idempotency or another concrete duplicate-prevention mechanism.
Respect Retry-After or equivalent rate-limit guidance where appropriate; never retry indefinitely or aggressively.
Use a fallback only when semantically acceptable; never hide a correctness failure behind a convenient default.
Caller cancellation is not a transient failure: do not classify it as one or turn it into repeated outbound attempts.
Filter and project in the database when practical, avoid unnecessary round trips, over-fetching and N+1, paginate potentially large result sets.

For the SQL Server baseline, appsettings.Development.json provides a usable local Development connection string when it contains no secret credentials; credential-bearing values come from user-secrets or another approved local secret mechanism.
An empty Development database receives a small deterministic representative seed dataset covering meaningful entity states and relationships.
Development seeding is an Infrastructure/bootstrap concern that may use AppDbContext directly without Application repositories or IUnitOfWork.

Substantial seed construction lives in a dedicated internal seeder (e.g. Persistence/Seeding/DbSeeder.cs) behind a narrow Infrastructure initialization extension, not in Program.cs, DbContext configuration, entity configurations or migrations.
Automatic development seeding runs only in Development, never automatically in Production; the seeder is never test setup.
The seeder does not call Database.Migrate() or EnsureCreated() or otherwise create/upgrade schema; migrations are applied separately before seeding.
When representative data exists, leave it unchanged: no synchronization, repair, upgrade, overwrite or recreation of an existing Development database; developers recreate local databases explicitly.
Seed entities preserve current Domain invariants and valid relationships; prefer readable deterministic examples over exhaustive/random combinations.
Authentication architecture changes are Reserved.
Use parameterized database access (EF Core LINQ, supported parameterization of raw SQL, Dapper or ADO.NET); never build SQL by concatenating untrusted input.

Default to explicit, reviewable authorization (global/fallback policies, attributes, endpoint configuration); anonymous access is deliberate and visible; avoid redundant [Authorize] when a secure global policy already expresses intent.
Do not implement custom token or password security, password hashing or reset-token cryptography when ASP.NET Core authentication/Identity covers the requirement.
For Bearer/OIDC validate what the actual issuer requires (issuer, audience where applicable, signature/signing authority, lifetime); never disable validation to make a token work.
Authentication failures do not expose detail that unnecessarily reveals secrets or account state; login avoids account-enumeration leaks where relevant.

No custom cryptography when a well-reviewed platform mechanism is appropriate; Data Protection suits application-generated protected payloads, not universal database encryption (use storage/database/platform encryption per requirement).
The narrowest CORS policy satisfying actual browser-client requirements; never combine credentialed cross-origin requests with an unrestricted origin policy.
Do not treat client-provided file metadata such as MIME type as authoritative when handling or a security decision depends on actual content.
NUnit for backend automated tests; in an established project deliberately using another framework follow it; do not introduce a second test framework without a concrete reason.

Choose the narrowest meaningful test level (unit for isolated logic; integration when framework wiring, HTTP, EF Core, persistence, serialization, authentication or component interaction is the subject); no fixed ratio.
WebApplicationFactory-based integration tests when routing, binding, middleware, authentication, DI, repositories, EF Core or persistence is what the test must prove.

Tests verify observable behavior, not implementation details (no private methods, exact internal call sequences, specific implementation classes or incidental refactoring details; no reproduced algorithm); interaction verification only when the interaction is the specified behavior.
Explicit declarative cases (e.g. [TestCase] rows) for small finite input/state spaces instead of loops, branching, LINQ or generated case machinery.
Descriptive test names communicating scenario/condition and expected behavior (e.g. MethodOrScenario_Condition_ExpectedBehavior) unless an established convention exists.
Do not generate low-value tests merely to increase coverage percentage.

Tests are deterministic, order-independent and isolated from Production and Development data, uncontrolled external systems and shared mutable state, and do not rely on wall-clock timing when TimeProvider can make time deterministic; never connect automated tests to Production data.
Tests start from a known state and own their setup; they do not depend on development seeding or test execution order.
Use the actual database provider when relational/provider behavior matters (Testcontainers optional); never claim provider fidelity from a different provider, including EF Core InMemory.
Test projects do not reference production projects more broadly than their test scope requires and follow the inward dependency discipline.
Adding or updating a package runs the add-dependency workflow (version, deprecation, vulnerability and license checks).
Add a dependency only for a concrete current requirement; no packages for hypothetical future use; an approved conditional technology is added only when its capability is actually needed.

Use NuGet Central Package Management: versions in Directory.Packages.props; project PackageReference entries versionless by default (a VersionOverride needs a concrete, reported reason) and never duplicating centrally managed versions.
Keep each package reference in the narrowest project that requires it; do not add a package to every project merely because they share a solution.
npm is the package manager for the Angular workspace unless the project deliberately adopts another; build and test tooling goes in devDependencies unless there is a concrete reason.
Keep package-lock.json consistent with every dependency change.

Physical structure follows actual responsibilities: no speculative projects, infrastructure, empty trees or generic Common/Helpers/Utils buckets; create a project, directory or documentation folder only when it holds real content with a cohesive, nameable responsibility.
Never hardcode or commit real secrets, credentials, private keys, access/refresh tokens or production connection strings in source-controlled files, example configuration included.

A local secret mechanism such as dotnet user-secrets for development and environment-specific injection or a managed secret store appropriate to the hosting platform for deployed environments; do not assume an unchosen cloud provider.

Treat data crossing the trusted boundary as untrusted (HTTP requests, uploads, external responses when assumptions matter, message payloads, identifiers and filters) and validate it at the layer that owns the assumption.
Authorization is enforced on the server; route guards, hidden/disabled buttons and client checks are UX, not a security boundary.
Production traffic carrying credentials or sensitive data uses TLS, respecting hosting topology (in-app HTTP-to-HTTPS redirection not required when deployment provides the secure boundary).
Never disable certificate validation to make an integration work.

Never log passwords, tokens, private keys, authentication secrets or full payment credentials; avoid PII without a concrete need permitted by privacy policy; prefer technical identifiers; log level does not make sensitive data safe.
Do not serialize arbitrary request bodies, domain objects or sensitive payloads into logs by default; log minimal useful non-sensitive context.
Security-sensitive authorization, permission and required-control checks fail safely; failures never silently turn into success.
A required security control that cannot be configured correctly does not fall back to an insecure mode; prefer visible startup/configuration failure.
Modern standalone Angular APIs for new code (no NgModules for ordinary new features unless an integration/legacy dependency requires them), organized primarily by feature.

Feature-oriented structure: no application-wide technical buckets (components/, services/, models/) spreading a feature, no empty architecture folders; feature code stays in its feature; core/shared small; do not move code to shared merely because two components of one feature use it.
Pages and components focus on presentation and UI orchestration; trivial presentation logic is not moved into services merely to shrink components.

Backend communication lives in explicit feature data-access services or another HTTP boundary; no HttpClient calls scattered through components; never import backend Domain entities (frontend API models follow the HTTP contract).
Functional interceptors for new code, limited to cross-cutting concerns; never feature business logic in an interceptor.
Signals for synchronous local UI state; RxJS when async streams, HTTP composition, cancellation or event pipelines express behavior more clearly; no mechanical conversions.
Simple component, signal or feature-service state before any state-management library.
Avoid manual nested RxJS subscriptions; prefer composition operators when they express behavior clearly.
A manual subscription from framework-managed code has its lifetime tied to the component/service lifecycle using current Angular facilities.
Route-level lazy loading for meaningful features; not for every tiny component.
Follow the documented API error contract: centralize reusable ProblemDetails parsing when practical; never infer business behavior from arbitrary human-readable exception messages.
Reactive forms for non-trivial forms when useful; frontend validation is UX and backend validation, data integrity and security enforcement remain authoritative.
When browser cookies carry authentication credentials automatically, include CSRF protection; do not assume Angular removes the risk.
Choose browser token storage by the application's threat model; never claim one storage mechanism is universally secure; tokens are never logged.

The NuGet packages Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Polly, Polly.Extensions.Http, Serilog.Sinks.Elasticsearch and FluentValidation.AspNetCore are reported as errors (deprecated; use Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience, Elastic.Serilog.Sinks, FluentValidation.DependencyInjectionExtensions).
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-004 requires a deprecation check before installation and DEP-020/DEP-010 set defaults, but no oracle policy turns specific packages into hard errors irrespective of an explicit decision.

normative_action: Central Package Management: Directory.Packages.props must set ManagePackageVersionsCentrally true and must exist at the repository root when .csproj files exist; a PackageReference carrying a Version is an error; a VersionOverride gets a notice that it needs a concrete, reported reason.

Pinned verified versions: a PackageVersion with an empty, floating (*) or range version is an error and a prerelease gets a notice (allowed only when explicitly requested); package.json dependency specs that are empty, *, latest, x or contain * are errors.
exceptions: Caret/tilde ranges are not flagged; prerelease allowed when explicitly requested.

normative_action: MediatR (mediator organization not adopted) and AutoMapper (mapping framework other than the approved one) get notices that they require an approved decision; direct Polly gets a notice that it is an explicit exception whose reason must be documented.

@ngrx/*, @ngxs/*, axios, lodash, lodash-es, bootstrap, ngx-bootstrap, @ng-bootstrap/ng-bootstrap, tailwindcss and primeng in package.json get a notice that they are not added by default and need a concrete requirement.
modality: MUST NOT by default (manifest check notice)

normative_action: Build/test tooling (@angular/cli, @angular-devkit/*, @angular/build, @angular/compiler-cli, typescript, vitest, @vitest/*, jsdom, @playwright/test, karma*, jasmine*, @types/*, eslint*, @eslint/*, prettier) in runtime dependencies gets a notice (belongs in devDependencies); a package.json without an adjacent package-lock.json gets a notice to commit a consistent lockfile.

A production project may reference only inward layers (Domain: none; Application: Domain; Infrastructure: Application, Domain; Api: Application, Infrastructure, Domain); other production references and production -> test-project references are errors.
exceptions: References to unrecognized projects get a notice instead.

normative_action: A project name not following backend/<Name>.<Layer>, or a reference to a project that is not a recognized layer, gets a notice that new production projects are Reserved.

A test project referencing a production layer outside its typical scope (Domain.Tests -> Domain; Application.Tests -> Application, Domain; Infrastructure.Tests -> Infrastructure, Application, Domain; IntegrationTests -> Api) gets a notice to confirm the test scope requires it.
Every instruction artifact carries the first-line header 'Kind
why_extra_or_uncertain: Loading' with a known Kind and Scope; its Kind must match its location/mechanism (CLAUDE.md OP, register DEC, CUSTOM_SETTINGS IN, rules STD, agents WF, hooks/scripts/root build files ENF; skills WF or KNW); OP/DEC load always and IN is read as input; no Level/Capability/Slot/Facet/Contract/Module fields, no numbered or level-ordered directories, no capability contracts/manifests/slots/facets, no unclassified files under .claude/ or docs/architecture/.

normative_action: Standards live directly in .claude/rules/<scope>/<topic>.md for scopes common, backend, backend-tests, frontend, delivery; the header Scope equals the directory; STD loads path-scoped with non-empty paths whose globs stay inside the scope territory (backend: backend/, root .NET build files, global.json, *.slnx; backend-tests: backend/ and containing Tests; frontend: frontend/; delivery: Docker/Compose/CI paths); standards contain no numbered procedures or Step/Procedure headings (procedures belong in workflows).
why_extra_or_uncertain: Rule-organization and loading discipline of the template; not a V2 policy.

normative_action: Skill and agent structure: skill frontmatter name equals the directory and has a concrete description (20+ characters); KNW skills load on demand and stay model-invocable; WF skills load as workflows; the required workflows (development-workflow, project-structure, verify, code-review, build-fix, custom-settings, git-workflow, security-scan, add-dependency, architecture-decision, delivery-pipeline, template-maintenance) and knowledge skills (ef-core, http-api, aspnet-error-handling, dotnet-testing, logging, httpclient-factory, configuration, dependency-injection, caching, swagger, api-versioning, health-check, docker, ci-cd, angular, modern-csharp, authentication) exist; template-maintenance is user-only (disable-model-invocation: true); private references have their skill's Kind and state that only that skill reads them; retired skill names (testing, error-handling, serilog, resilience) are not used; agents' frontmatter name equals the file name and they load as agents.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Template inventory and packaging rules; the oracle prescribes no skill inventory or metadata.

normative_action: Knowledge skills and their private references must not contain normative wording (must, never, requires approval) on a line without an owner reference (rules/, CLAUDE.md or a D-xx decision ID); the rule must be moved to its standard and pointed to.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Instruction-authoring rule (normative statements only in owners); no V2 policy constrains where normative wording may appear.

normative_action: Exactly one decision register (docs/architecture/decision-register.md) carries Kind DEC and CLAUDE.md imports exactly it; register rows are 'D-xx
why_extra_or_uncertain: Affects' with unique IDs, a non-empty Decision that does not depend on rules/skills/scripts, existing Affects targets of Kind STD/KNW/WF/ENF and Details-in targets also listed in Affects; any artifact citing D-xx must be listed in that decision's Affects; decision entries are defined only in the register; no other artifact may restate a decision (8-word overlap) — cite the ID instead.

normative_action: References must resolve: backticked file/skill/agent references and '§ section' references must point to existing targets and headings; unknown hyphenated skill/agent names in skill contexts are errors; skill-private references are used only by their own skill.
exceptions: Placeholders, commands and plain hyphenated words are skipped.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Referential-integrity rule of the instruction system; not a V2 policy.

normative_action: Manual tool invocations in instruction files must be root-aware: node "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/.claude/..." instead of a command relative to the current directory.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Command-portability rule of the template; not a V2 policy.

normative_action: Hook configuration: every hook is a command hook in exec form (executable-only command, args [${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.claude/hooks/<script>, <event>] with the script present and handling the event), no variable expansion in arguments, a positive timeout; PreToolUse (pre-tool-use, Bash/PowerShell), PostToolUse (post-tool-use, Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit/Bash/PowerShell), PostToolUseFailure (Bash/PowerShell) and Stop must be registered; only the PreToolUse policy hook may set onFailure, and it must be 'block' (fail closed).
why_extra_or_uncertain: Enforcement-configuration invariants of the template; no V2 policy requires hooks.

normative_action: Use the approved technology from the decision register and a conditional technology only when its capability is now needed; a new major library or framework, or a replacement of an approved technology, is Reserved — stop with a Decision Request.

When resilience is required prefer Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience for HttpClient and Microsoft.Extensions.Resilience for general pipelines; a direct Polly reference or Polly API configuration is an explicit exception needing a documented reason why the Microsoft.Extensions APIs cannot express the requirement.

When Controller API versioning has been explicitly adopted use the Controller integration of Asp.Versioning (e.g. Asp.Versioning.Mvc with Asp.Versioning.Mvc.ApiExplorer); do not add it before versioning is adopted.

Register FluentValidation validators with FluentValidation.DependencyInjectionExtensions; do not add a deprecated or legacy ASP.NET automatic-validation integration package without a concrete requirement.
exceptions: concrete requirement (but FluentValidation.AspNetCore is a hard manifest error, EXTRA-K0-0009)
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-010 makes FluentValidation the standard library but prescribes no registration package; no oracle policy restricts the automatic-validation integration package.

normative_action: For every NuGet or npm addition or update determine the latest stable version compatible with target framework/runtime and peers, verify it from the registry (not memory, examples or older content) and avoid prerelease or floating versions unless explicitly requested; 'latest' means latest stable compatible.

Before installation check, for the exact selected version, deprecation status, known vulnerabilities from advisory data and the license from official registry metadata (and upstream text when necessary); permissive licenses are generally suitable; free download does not make a package acceptable.

Paid/commercial packages are not installed automatically: present explicit choices with reasonable free alternatives (or say none exist), never substitute silently; strong copyleft, dual licensing, source-available/custom or unclear licenses are not adopted automatically — explain the concern and alternatives; no legal conclusions beyond the published license.
NuGet installs add the version to Directory.Packages.props and a versionless PackageReference to the narrowest project that needs it.
npm installs go into the Angular workspace with the right category (--save-dev for build/test tooling) and keep package-lock.json consistent.
Never use --force or --legacy-peer-deps merely to bypass incompatible peer dependencies; resolve the actual compatibility problem.
After a dependency change restore and build the affected projects and run check-dependencies.
Inspect vulnerability information (dotnet package list --vulnerable --include-transitive; npm audit) with context; do not upgrade or replace unrelated packages because of a finding.
Remove a dependency that is no longer used when that is part of the current change and safe to verify; do not leave dead references behind.
trigger_scope: Changes that make a dependency unused
exceptions: Not during unrelated cleanup of a narrowly scoped task.
why_extra_or_uncertain: No oracle policy obliges removing packages made unused by a change (RUN-010 concerns only unused usings).

normative_action: Do not perform unrelated dependency cleanup during a narrowly scoped task.
The add-dependency output reports package, selected version and why, license, deprecation and vulnerability status, approval obtained (if needed), files changed and the verification result.
why_extra_or_uncertain: WF-009 covers verification reporting only; the per-package report content is an additional workflow duty.

normative_action: Use Angular Material components consistently for common UI primitives where they meet the requirement; wrap a Material component in a custom abstraction only for a concrete reason.
When OpenAPI client generation is adopted keep generated code separate from handwritten feature logic and regenerate it when the API contract changes.

Frontend test targets are meaningful component behavior, validation, data-access request mapping, important route/auth behavior and complex reactive state, not Angular framework internals; run the workspace's configured test runner; E2E covers a small number of important workflows unless more is required; the same behavior is not duplicated at every level.
Start with route lazy loading and sensible rendering and data access; specialized memoization, virtual scrolling or custom change-detection work follows an identified need.
Adopting API versioning is Reserved (D-15).
why_extra_or_uncertain: API-013 forbids versioning without a concrete need and DEP-017 makes the package conditional; neither requires explicit approval once the need exists.

normative_action: Classify a decision by stating it and its options and applying CLAUDE.md decision classes: Decided follows the existing entry, Delegated is decided and proceeds, only Reserved decisions or changes to accepted ones continue in this workflow.
Present a Decision Request (title, context, 2-3 options incl. keeping the current decision, recommendation, Blocked work, Proceeding-with compliant work) and wait for approval.
An explicit user instruction to adopt a specific option counts as approval; in an autonomous or headless run continue only with the 'Proceeding with' path and report the request as unresolved.
When a new behavioral rule is approved update the durable source of truth, including SPECIFICATION.md when appropriate.
An approved tunable value is recorded in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md and then synchronized with custom-settings.
An approved project or architecture decision is recorded as a register entry (add or update).

Decision propagation: find everything a decision touches via its register entry and Affects list; after approval edit every artifact in Affects so each keeps only its own responsibility (standards cite the ID, knowledge adjusts technique, workflows commands, enforcement checks such as deny-lists) and keep the Affects list current.
why_extra_or_uncertain: GOV-017 requires approval of Reserved changes but no Affects-driven propagation procedure across instruction artifacts.

normative_action: When rationale, alternatives or consequences need more than the register sentence add an ADR docs/decisions/NNNN-<slug>.md (Status, Date, Register, Context, Decision, Alternatives considered, Consequences) cited in Details in; superseding marks the old ADR 'Superseded by NNNN' and replaces the register entry — never two active entries for one choice; register IDs are stable and never reused.
why_extra_or_uncertain: No oracle policy requires ADRs, ADR structure or superseding bookkeeping.

normative_action: Changes to .claude/ instruction files are instruction-system maintenance: ask the user to run /template-maintenance for structural changes and run check-instructions after any instruction edit.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Template-maintenance routing; no V2 policy governs instruction-file maintenance.

normative_action: The architecture-decision output is the Decision Request (when pending) or the recorded outcome: register entry, ADR path if any, artifacts updated, checker result.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Workflow-specific report content beyond WF-009.

normative_action: Choose the authentication scheme by the actual application (Bearer/OIDC for an SPA calling an API; cookies for server-rendered apps; Identity when the app owns local users and needs account management; external OIDC/OAuth when identity is delegated); a User entity or profile management alone does not call for Identity, and an API needing authentication does not call for custom JWT issuance when an existing identity provider issues tokens.
Build-fix restores the affected scope to green without hiding failures, weakening behavior or introducing unrelated changes.

Reproduce and diagnose the actual failure (narrowest reproducing command with the repository's actual .slnx/projects; complete output read and grouped by root cause) before editing; no guessing; fix root causes and the highest-leverage cause first.

Small bounded iterations: rerun the narrowest failing verification after each meaningful fix, expand only after the focused failure is resolved; stop and reassess when progress stalls (same root failure after different fixes, growing unrelated failures, incompatible toolchain, missing infrastructure, unresolvable package compatibility, undeterminable behavior); never repeat variants of the same failed guess.

Never weaken, delete, skip or suppress relevant tests, compiler, TypeScript, lint or analyzer failures merely to pass; do not weaken a strong assertion or delete/skip a failing test because fixing it is inconvenient.

Preserve architecture and project conventions while fixing; a green build obtained by violating architecture (e.g. Application -> Infrastructure references, DbContext in Application, business logic in a Controller, Angular-only authorization, scattered HTTP calls) is not a successful repair.
Determine the affected scope (backend, Angular, both, contract/client generation, dependencies, toolchain) and do not run unrelated build systems merely because they exist.

For Angular inspect package.json first and use scripts that actually exist; do not invent script names or assume a test runner (an existing project may deliberately use another runner than the D-09 default).
exceptions: Applies the CI-scoped WF-018 rule to local repair.

normative_action: Never solve a dependency problem with an invalid project reference (e.g. Application -> Infrastructure).

Frontend repairs do not convert code to any to silence TypeScript, disable strict mode, suppress template diagnostics without understanding, add NgModules to work around standalone configuration problems, replace framework APIs speculatively, or add another state-management or HTTP library to bypass a local issue.

For full-stack/contract failures determine the authoritative contract; do not patch both sides into inconsistent shapes merely to compile; with OpenAPI generation verify the backend contract, regenerate the client normally, review the generated changes, then fix handwritten frontend code.
If expected behavior intentionally changed, update the test to express the new contract and confirm the change was actually requested.
During package-related repair respect Central Package Management and do not delete package-lock.json reflexively.

For upgrade fallout distinguish compile errors from runtime behavior changes, check official migration documentation, update obsolete APIs deliberately (no fabricated replacement APIs when they can be verified), preserve architecture/behavior and perform no additional unrelated upgrade.
Do not change the repository's declared SDK, Node, framework or language version merely because the local machine differs; report an unavailable toolchain instead of editing source to compensate.

When generated output is wrong or its source changed, fix the authoritative source (OpenAPI document, generator input, EF Core model, build configuration) and regenerate; do not manually patch disposable generated output unless intentionally maintained as source.

If a fix introduces new failures decide whether they reveal a legitimate dependency or revert/correct the fix; never leave the repository knowingly worse; do not clean up unrelated pre-existing failures unless they block verification or the user asks.

A repair is complete when the affected scope is green (builds, affected tests, consistent contracts, no known new regression, no accidental workaround); diagnosis probes follow verify § 4; then run verify for the final pass when appropriate.

Report repairs with backend build, frontend build and tests as PASS / NOT RUN / NOT APPLICABLE plus failure, root cause, changes and remaining issues; do not claim the problem is fixed while a known relevant failure remains.
Caching EF tracked entities across Unit of Work boundaries is listed as a mistake to avoid.
why_extra_or_uncertain: No oracle policy and no K0 standard forbids caching tracked entities across Unit of Work scopes; the knowledge skill adds this restriction as a named mistake.

normative_action: An optional local formatter does not become a mandatory CI gate without the project adopting that policy.
Frontend CI runs the unit-test and lint scripts the workspace actually defines, adding them only when the project defines them.

Provide CI test services (SQL Server, PostgreSQL, Redis, brokers) only when tests require them; the generic template hardcodes no database provider and the test environment stays isolated from Development and Production data.
Automatic dependency updates in CI need explicit adoption; dependency-audit findings are treated per the project's security policy.
Store or publish only artifacts later stages need; build and publish container images from CI only when container deployment is part of the project.
Migration scripts or bundles may be generated in CI and are executed by an explicit deployment step.
Code review examines the actual changed behavior and reports concrete defects or risks; it is not the completion checklist — verify runs the final build/test/diff verification.

Prioritize findings: correctness; security and authorization; data integrity and persistence; architectural boundary violations; concurrency and integration; missing meaningful tests; maintainability; credible performance; do not elevate style above defects or bury important findings.

Establish the reviewed scope, read changed code plus callers/contracts/dependencies (never isolated lines), identify intended behavior and tests, read the standards for touched scopes and load the knowledge skill for each changed technology area.

Check specification conformance in both directions (approved CUSTOM_SETTINGS values are intended behavior): flag missing/weakened required behavior and unapproved product behavior (new limits, reserved names/values, observable string-comparison semantics incl. database configuration/framework defaults, new required fields, extra workflow restrictions, extra user-visible validation); approved recorded details are not drift; internal details are not product behavior.
Look for correctness defects (conditions, state transitions, null/empty, async/cancellation, error mapping, lifetimes, side effects, races) and report a failure only with a plausible execution path.

Check backend changes against the architecture standard (Domain independence, Application free of Infrastructure/EF Core, thin Controllers, Application Services, specific repositories, no DbContext/DbSet/IQueryable leaks, no independent repository commits, IUnitOfWork commit boundary), proportionality (no unapproved Rich Domain, DDD, CQRS/MediatR/VSA, extra layers, project-wide Result) and frontend changes against the Angular standard without applying backend project-boundary rules mechanically.

Do not report a violation merely because the implementation differs from a pattern the project has not adopted; do not require unadopted patterns (MediatR, CQRS, VSA, Minimal APIs, Rich Domain Models, Domain Events, generic repositories).

When relevant check commit/transaction behavior, destructive changes, raw SQL parameterization, authorization, trust boundaries, secrets, sensitive logging, concurrency, migrations and cache consistency against the standards, and the seeder obligation for model/migration changes affecting seeded entities; use the full security-scan only for a requested audit, a materially security-sensitive change or a concrete finding.
Check external calls for cancellation, time limits, idempotency, retry safety, failure translation and lifetime; do not demand retries for operations that are not safe to retry.
Check that changed behavior has useful maintained coverage; for bug fixes look for the regression test; confirm probe preservation; do not demand duplicate tests when equivalent coverage exists.
Report performance only with a credible reason; do not recommend compiled queries, pooling, caching, ValueTask or similar optimizations speculatively.
Review needs no MCP server or specific analyzer; tool output is evidence, not authority — read the code before turning a warning into a finding.
Each finding states severity, location, what is wrong, why it matters and the smallest fix, ordered by severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low).
Do not manufacture findings to populate categories; with no meaningful findings say so and name important unverifiable areas; no filler praise.
Review discipline: do not rewrite working code during review unless asked, report tooling-owned formatting, demand personal style preferences or assume every warning is a bug.
Numbers in configuration examples are illustrative; choose retry counts, timeouts and limits from actual integration and deployment requirements.
A new or changed setting not already defined by the specification or approved behavior must be confirmed as approved; otherwise raise a Decision Request first.
Check SPECIFICATION.md for conflicts before synchronizing a setting.
Record the setting with a stable descriptive name and purpose; do not record framework defaults the project has not intentionally overridden.

Search for the old value, setting name, validators/DTO constraints, Domain/Application checks, mapping constraints, frontend validation/UI hints, tests/test data, docs/examples and mirrored configuration; separate coincidences; update every affected implementation, validation, configuration, test, documentation and mirrored frontend/backend surface, preferring one normal source over duplicated literals.
Where frontend and backend expose the same constraint, backend validation stays authoritative and frontend validation/messages follow it for UX.

When a setting change affects schema constraints, indexes, column lengths or other persistence metadata: update the EF Core mapping, create the appropriate migration per the migration workflow (edit an uncommitted migration only when normal; never casually alter existing migrations), verify Development seeding remains valid and update provider-sensitive tests when needed.

Verify settings changes: search for stale references, build affected backend/frontend, run relevant tests, verify persistence changes, re-check SPECIFICATION.md, run verify; changing one literal alone does not establish synchronization and the setting is not declared synchronized until every surface is updated and verified.
Containers are optional (D-14): introduce Docker or container publishing only when the project has adopted containers.
Inspect what actually exists before writing pipeline or container files; do not assume PostgreSQL, Redis, Docker or frontend tooling; add stages for the actual project, not generic boilerplate.

CI definitions are kept in source control, reproduce the repository's supported build and test commands and never hide build or test failures (no suppressed or skipped failing tests to permit deployment).
Frontend CI uses scripts that exist in package.json (never invented) and npm ci whenever a maintained lockfile supports it, not reflexive npm install.

Production database migrations are not applied automatically from normal startup by default; a production migration is an explicit, controlled deployment step with approved credentials that fails visibly (scripts/bundles may be generated earlier in CI); Development seeding never runs in Production.

Verify a pipeline: restore from a clean environment, build backend and frontend (when present), run configured tests, no developer-machine state, no exposed secrets, expected artifacts; for container changes build the image, start the app and check port/configuration, non-root execution and health-probe integration.
The delivery-pipeline output lists files changed, stages and the commands they run, what was verified and any hosting-platform assumption still needing confirmation.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Workflow-specific report content beyond WF-009's verification reporting.

normative_action: Use interface-to-implementation registration at architectural boundaries (concrete registration for implementation-only helpers); prefer explicit registration in small/medium applications; keyed services, factories, decorators, Scrutor and convention scanning only for actual composition problems (Scrutor not for a single decoration; scan the owning assembly).
For a new application or substantial feature read SPECIFICATION.md before planning or implementing, and CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md when it holds values.
Check the request against the challenge obligation and the product-source rules (gaps, string semantics, tunable values) before implementing.

Inspect the relevant existing code (code, callers, contracts, tests, conventions) before any non-trivial change; apply standards and knowledge for touched areas; when planning before files are opened, read the standards for the scopes to be changed; load the knowledge skill for each technology involved; route sub-tasks to their workflows.
Stay within the requested scope.
For a meaningful bug with plausible recurrence add a regression test that fails before and passes after the fix, unless equivalent coverage exists.

Whenever a Domain or persistence change affects seeded entities (new required/removed/renamed properties, changed relationships, required related entities, enum/status values, meaningful states, invariants) update the development seeder in the same change; recreating an empty Development database must yield valid representative data; already seeded rows are not patched.

Treat EF Core migrations as source code: review every generated migration before committing (destructive changes, column recreation, data migrations, indexes, foreign keys, delete behavior) and review the seeder together with any migration affecting seeded entities.
Performance-motivated changes: identify the bottleneck, preserve behavior, simplest effective optimization, add/maintain tests, benchmark or profile non-obvious/complex optimizations.
Classify a public API contract change as compatible or breaking; a breaking change to a relied-on contract follows the versioning rules and is Reserved.

Deprecating an externally consumed API version: mark it in versioning metadata, document the replacement, communicate a realistic migration and removal timeline, keep the old version working for the promised period, and do not remove it without considering the published support contract.
For substantial feature work or a newly implemented application run code-review (agent code-reviewer) before final verification.
Before declaring implementation complete run verify with checks appropriate to scope and risk.
The development-workflow output states what changed and why, the Delegated decisions taken, Decision Requests raised or still unresolved, and the verification report.
why_extra_or_uncertain: WF-009 covers verification reporting; reporting every Delegated decision taken and every Decision Request is an additional duty.

normative_action: Test the risks that matter and build test infrastructure only for a concrete testing need (no enterprise-sized harness for a small project, no generic test-data framework for a few simple objects, no snapshot library by default).

Turn temporary behavioral probes (HTTP requests, shell/PowerShell scripts, ad-hoc test methods, manual database checks) into maintained tests (e.g. an ad-hoc curl becomes a WebApplicationFactory test); confirm an existing test really covers the behavior instead of adding a duplicate; review probes before keeping them.
Register EF Core and persistence implementations in Infrastructure with the provider the project actually uses, not one that merely appears in an example.
EF Core interceptors fit infrastructure-level cross-cutting behavior with a clear benefit (e.g. auditing); business behavior does not belong in them.
Fire-and-forget EF Core asynchronous operations are listed as a mistake to avoid.
why_extra_or_uncertain: RUN-002 forbids blocking async I/O and ARC-022 governs lifetimes; no oracle policy (and no K0 standard) forbids un-awaited database operations.

normative_action: Repository-changing Git operations happen only when explicitly requested and parallel work uses separate branches or worktrees; completing an implementation is not a request to commit, push or merge.
Never discard, overwrite, reset, clean or otherwise destroy user work to make a Git operation easier.

Before any repository-changing operation inspect the relevant state (git status, git diff, git diff --cached) and use the minimum operation required; never silently clean unrelated working-tree changes.

Before committing inspect the staged diff and include only the requested logical change; do not stage unrelated modified files or clean them up; prefer one logical change per commit with implementation and its tests together, no artificial tiny commits, no combined unrelated fixes and refactors.
Follow the repository's branch-naming convention (defaults feature/, fix/, refactor/, test/, docs/, chore/ with meaningful names) and do not rename an existing user branch to satisfy a convention.

Keep each worktree focused on its branch; one branch is not checked out in several normal worktrees; before removing a worktree verify its changes are preserved and never remove one holding uncommitted user work.
Before pushing confirm the intended branch and understood working/staged state, ensure relevant verification completed and avoid pushing unrelated local commits.
Never force-push a shared branch unless the user explicitly requests history rewriting and the consequences are understood.
Treat main, master and other protected or shared branches as non-rewritable.
why_extra_or_uncertain: GOV-015 allows history-changing operations on explicit request; declaring main/master non-rewritable is a stricter, unconditional restriction.

normative_action: For merge/rebase follow the repository/team convention or the user's explicit request; inspect local uncommitted work first and never automatically stash, reset or discard it; resolve conflicts from intended combined behavior, not mechanically ours/theirs; run relevant verification afterwards.
Run verify before preparing a PR; one focused purpose without accidental unrelated changes; never claim checks that were not run.
A PR describes what changed, why, how it was verified and any compatibility or migration notes.
why_extra_or_uncertain: No oracle policy fixes PR description content.

normative_action: git reset --hard, git clean, git push --force/--force-with-lease, branch deletion and rebasing shared history are high-risk: run them only when explicitly requested (or required by an approved workflow, see UNCERTAIN-K0-0002) and inspect what will be lost or rewritten first.
High-risk Git operations may run when 'required by an approved workflow', not only when explicitly requested.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Open question: GOV-015 requires an explicit request for repository-changing Git operations; whether 'required by an approved workflow' means a workflow the user explicitly requested (entailed) or allows destructive operations without a specific request (relaxation) is not determinable from the text.

normative_action: Resilience policies match failure and operation semantics: add a mechanism only for an identified failure scenario, configure it through the Microsoft.Extensions resilience APIs, the standard handler is not mandatory for every client, and handlers with overlapping strategies are not stacked.

Do not wrap normal EF Core operations in a generic application-level retry pipeline; prefer the provider's EF Core execution strategy for transient retry and handle transaction/retry interaction per provider guidance; HTTP retry policies are not database policies.
why_extra_or_uncertain: RUN-016 limits retries to safe operations and DEP-020 sets resilience package defaults; no oracle policy forbids application-level retry pipelines around database calls or prescribes provider execution strategies (the oracle treats database-retry examples as technique, EXC-007).

normative_action: DelegatingHandlers are for genuine HTTP pipeline concerns (authorization header acquisition, correlation/context propagation, request signing), not business decisions.

Per-request values such as dynamic access tokens go on the request or through a handler; mutating a shared client's DefaultRequestHeaders concurrently for request-specific values is a race (stable media-type headers may be configured on the client).
why_extra_or_uncertain: RUN-005 governs client lifetime only; no oracle policy restricts how request-specific headers are applied.

normative_action: Confirm the configured language version supports a feature; changing LangVersion or the target framework to use newer syntax is a decision, not a silent edit (language or framework version changes need approval).
When explicitly asked to modernize: preserve behavior, keep the change focused, favor readability, build and test afterwards, keep architecture refactoring out of syntax modernization.
Controllers are thin ASP.NET Core Controllers; no Minimal API endpoint groups unless explicitly requested.
Backend tests never go into a separate top-level tests/ directory; integration tests exercise the other layers transitively through the API host.

For a new application install the packages each baseline decision names plus the scaffold packages (Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Design where migrations are created; provider in Infrastructure with Api as migrations startup; Console sink for a simple local logging baseline; NUnit3TestAdapter and Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk in test projects) through add-dependency with versions resolved at install time.

Create the Angular workspace with the latest stable release supported by the selected Node.js via the current CLI (CLI-selected compatible Angular/TypeScript/RxJS; no independent TypeScript upgrade), selecting standalone APIs, strict mode, routing, SCSS and zoneless mode when supported; add Material/CDK via the CLI; configure the decided unit-test runner and add E2E tooling only under the E2E decision.

The solution layout is a target shape: create optional directories, projects and docs/ subdirectories only when needed (only when the corresponding documentation exists); do not make the repository match the diagram for its own sake.

The Angular workspace lives outside the .NET tree in frontend/ProjectName.Web/ and owns its package.json, package-lock.json, angular.json, tsconfig files, src/ and public/; do not impose an obsolete Angular directory structure when the current CLI generates a different supported one.

Angular unit/component tests stay in the workspace (usually colocated); E2E tests, when adopted, also stay in the workspace (e.g. frontend/ProjectName.Web/e2e/); Angular tests never go under backend/.
Directory.Build.props holds the shared settings of the shared-build decision (typically TargetFramework, Nullable, ImplicitUsings, analysis and compiler settings).

Scaffolding creates the repository-wide files global.json (pinning the intended supported .NET SDK line: current stable SDK of the target release with a chosen rollForward servicing policy), .editorconfig, .gitignore and README.md alongside the .slnx and Directory.*.props files.
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-022/DEP-023 cover the solution format and Directory.*.props; no oracle policy requires a global.json SDK pin, .editorconfig, .gitignore or README.md at scaffolding.

normative_action: No RC/preview SDK unless explicitly requested.

Docker files, deployment manifests, Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, messaging infrastructure and additional services are introduced only for a concrete requirement; optional infrastructure is not scaffolded because it may be useful later.
A new solution creates the Domain, Application, Infrastructure and Api projects under backend/ targeting the decided platform.

Create only useful test projects beside production projects under backend/ (typically Application.Tests and IntegrationTests; Domain.Tests only for non-trivial Domain behavior; Infrastructure.Tests only for a concrete need).

Verify scaffolding and structural changes: restore, build the .NET solution and the Angular app when present, run relevant tests, run check-dependencies, inspect the final tree, confirm the Development configuration is usable, then run verify; never report successful scaffolding for a solution that does not build; complete only when structure, references and stack match the scope with no speculative or unrelated changes.

Confirm a new assembly is justified (a new production project is Reserved), identify its responsibility, add only minimum references preserving dependency direction, update shared configuration when necessary, build and test.

Reorganize only for a concrete structural problem: inspect tree and references, preserve behavior, move in small reviewable steps, update namespaces/references consistently, avoid unrelated feature work, verify; do not force an established project to match the template without concrete value.

Not scaffolded by default: MediatR, CQRS handler trees, Vertical Slice Architecture, Domain Events, Specifications, SharedKernel, BuildingBlocks, EventBus, messaging, microservices, Kubernetes, cloud-specific projects, state-management frameworks, Docker files and deployment manifests — each needs an actual requirement and most are Reserved.

Security severity comes from exploitability, reachability, exposure, impact and context (confirmed findings separated from NEEDS VERIFICATION items), never from a suspicious pattern, raw CVSS score or OWASP category alone; a theoretical missing limit is not automatically High; findings carry severity, location, title, evidence, risk, impact, remediation and OWASP category when applicable.

Report concrete security risks evaluated against actual exposure, not generic advice or mechanical pattern matches (e.g. normal EF Core LINQ is not SQL injection), and never invent exploitability the code does not establish.

A security scan is an evidence-based static review, not a penetration test; state its limitations in the report and name security-sensitive workflows as threat-modeling or manual-review candidates instead of claiming the scan proves them secure.

The review does not depend on a specific MCP server, agent, analyzer, commercial scanner or other external tool; tooling is evidence, not the sole authority; scanner reports are confirmed against the code before reporting with appropriate confidence.

Inspect which surfaces exist and skip irrelevant checks instead of reporting them as failures; a full pre-release or requested audit reviews every applicable layer, a targeted change starts with affected layers and expands across security boundaries.

Layer status is PASS, FINDINGS, NOT APPLICABLE or NOT CHECKED — never PASS for an uninspected layer; the scan completes only when applicable layers were inspected, findings carry evidence, uncertain findings are labelled and limitations stated.

Recommend the smallest secure change consistent with the architecture; do not require mechanisms the project does not need, a new authentication system unnecessarily, custom cryptography, blanket encryption, [Authorize] on every action under a protecting global policy, security libraries merely to satisfy the scan, or disabling functionality a scanner cannot understand.

Swashbuckle Swagger UI is the developer-facing documentation/testing surface (configured in the API/composition layer); built-in AddOpenApi()/MapOpenApi() is not a replacement when the requirement is interactive Swagger UI testing.

After API changes verify Controller behavior, relevant integration tests and response metadata, start the API when startup/composition changed, confirm the Development Swagger UI loads, exercise representative endpoints when meaningful and preserve newly verified behavior in maintained tests.
Keep the always-loaded surface (CLAUDE.md, the register, skill descriptions) compact and move detail to the owner it belongs to.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Context-budget rule of the template; no V2 policy.

normative_action: When hooks or scripts change, exercise them with a sample payload (e.g. a pre-tool-use JSON for 'npm install lodash').
why_extra_or_uncertain: Template-maintenance testing duty; no V2 policy concerns hook scripts.

normative_action: Template maintenance summarizes what moved, the new owners and the checker result.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Workflow-specific report content; not a V2 policy.

normative_action: Verification produces evidence that the requested change is complete without obvious regressions, matched to scope and risk, without requiring tooling the repository has not configured.

Before choosing checks review the final changed-file set and diff: confirm scope (no accidental unrelated refactoring), remove accidental generated/build artifacts and secrets, and determine the affected areas.

If an ad-hoc or manual probe uniquely demonstrated the behavior, that behavior is represented by maintained automated coverage before completion unless equivalent coverage exists (confirmed); temporary probes are removed only afterwards; builds, compilers, formatters, static analysis and existing suites need no new tests.

Build the affected projects (targeted project or .slnx when appropriate; no --no-restore unless restore is complete; Angular build script defined in package.json); a build failure means the implementation is not complete.

Run relevant tests (Angular: the configured test script, no assumed runner; full suite for small solutions, affected projects then broader suite for large ones) and investigate every new relevant failure; never dismiss one as unrelated without checking.

For a new runnable application or substantial startup/configuration/persistence/full-stack change verify local Development startup (API host, Development endpoint, Swagger UI when exposed, configuration binding, database connectivity/initialization, frontend dev server, compatible API base URL and CORS); a successful build alone does not prove runtime composition.

Run architecture (check-dependencies plus review against the architecture standard; seeder obligation when the model changed), formatting/analyzer (when configured, without adding tools) and dependency/security checks (vulnerability inspection and changed secrets/authorization/SQL/CORS/TLS/logging/certificate validation) only when relevant; full security-scan only when warranted.

For every C# file created or modified by the task remove unused or redundant usings (including implicit/global duplicates unless needed for clarity) without unrelated repository-wide cleanup; check the changed files rather than assuming tooling removed every import.

Final diff review checks accidental unrelated edits, commented-out code, temporary logging, unintended TODO/FIXME, stale temporary tests/scripts, architecture drift, unapproved SPECIFICATION/CUSTOM_SETTINGS drift, stale artifacts after a settings change and manually verified behavior never preserved.

When verification fails identify the concrete failure, make the smallest fix, rerun affected verification (and build/tests when code changed) and repeat until green or genuine user input is required; never hide a known failure or declare completion while one remains; switch to build-fix for stubborn failures.

Report what was actually run using PASS, FAIL, NOT RUN or NOT APPLICABLE per area (backend build, frontend build, tests, runtime smoke, formatting/analyzers, architecture check, security/dependency scan, diff review); never imply an unchecked area passed.

Repository formatting and C# style configuration: UTF-8, final newline, trimmed trailing whitespace (not Markdown), 4-space indentation (2 for JSON/YAML/web/project files); file-scoped namespaces, System usings first and outside the namespace, IDE0005 unnecessary usings at warning severity; var when the type is apparent; modern syntax preferences; braces on new lines and when multiline; PascalCase types/members, camelCase parameters/locals and the Async suffix (suggestions).
trigger_scope: Editors, dotnet format and build analyzers
exceptions: Mostly suggestion/silent severities; IDE0005 is a warning.

normative_action: Instruction precedence: CLAUDE.md and the decision register govern every task; standards govern the files they cover; workflows own procedures; knowledge skills supply technique and never override a standard.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Instruction-layer precedence of the template design; the oracle defines policies, not a precedence order among instruction artifacts.
