normative_action: Product inputs (SPECIFICATION.md, CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md, feature specifications, task prompts) define product behavior and may request a decision change but never silently override CLAUDE.md, the decision register or a standard.
exceptions: Approved specification requirements count as Decided.

normative_action: Vocabulary: must / must not — a violation is a defect; default — deviation needs a concrete reason and must be reported; prefer / avoid — guidance; requires approval — a Reserved decision.
trigger_scope: All normative text and deviations from defaults
why_extra_or_uncertain: The oracle grades policies but defines no duty to report each deviation from a default; the reporting duty changes how every default binds.

normative_action: When SPECIFICATION.md is non-empty it is authoritative for project-specific functional requirements and observable product behavior (empty in the template intentionally).
Do not silently weaken, contradict or materially extend approved behavior and do not invent user-visible rules, limits, defaults, restrictions or workflows the product sources do not define.
If an omitted detail must be decided and materially affects observable behavior, propose the smallest reasonable option and ask for approval.
Routine internal implementation choices that do not change observable behavior are Delegated.

Observable string semantics (case sensitivity, collation, culture vs ordinal, normalization, trimming, uniqueness, lookup) are product behavior; when undefined by the product sources do not choose silently — ask for approval.
CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md owns approved project-level tunable limits and defaults (maximum lengths, page sizes, retention periods, numeric thresholds); SPECIFICATION.md owns behavioral intent.
SPECIFICATION.md and CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md must not contradict each other; on conflict stop and ask which source must be corrected.

Do not silently invent a tunable value that materially changes accepted input or observable behavior: propose it with its reason, get approval, record it in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md, then synchronize it (custom-settings).
CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md must not contain secrets, environment-specific connection details, package versions, HTTP status codes, ports, migration identifiers or incidental implementation constants.
The simplest maintainable solution with complexity proportional to current requirements and no speculative abstractions.
Do not introduce frameworks, libraries, infrastructure or architectural patterns without a concrete current need.
Keep changes focused on the requested scope and preserve existing behavior unless the task or approved specification requires a change.

Challenge before implementing: when a request raises a material concern (duplication, poor cohesion, trigger/loading problems, context cost, conflict with an accepted decision, unnecessary complexity) name it and propose an alternative first; never silently rewrite or ignore the requirement.

Decided: what is recorded in the register, the approved product sources or the established project structure is followed and not reopened without approval; use an approved technology instead of silently selecting an alternative.
Delegated: local, reversible choices with no material change to a boundary, dependency, accepted convention, public contract or observable behavior are decided without asking.
Reserved decisions require explicit approval unless the approved specification or established project structure already requires them.
Changing an accepted project or architecture decision, or replacing an approved baseline technology, is Reserved.
A new architectural style or pattern (Rich Domain Model or DDD tactical patterns, CQRS, mediators, VSA, event sourcing, microservices) is Reserved.
A new production project, layer or assembly is Reserved.
Persistence boundaries or persistence technology, including multiple DbContexts, are Reserved.
A new infrastructure category (messaging, background processing, distributed cache, search, external storage, external identity) is Reserved.
A new major library or framework is Reserved.
A project-wide convention or abstraction other code must follow (e.g. a project-wide Result model) is Reserved.
A breaking public API change is Reserved.
Product behavior or tunable values the product sources do not define are Reserved.

Unclear decisions are Reserved if any answer is yes: adds, removes or replaces a dependency, framework or infrastructure capability; changes a project, layer or reference boundary; establishes a convention other code must follow; changes observable behavior or a public contract; becomes expensive to reverse.
why_extra_or_uncertain: GOV-017 requires classification and ARC-020 lists consequential choices, but neither contains this test; its first question makes unclear dependency additions/removals approval-gated beyond DEP-001..DEP-005.

normative_action: For a Reserved decision raise a Decision Request (Context, Options, Recommendation, Blocked, Proceeding with) and wait; an explicit user instruction counts as approval; record every accepted decision through architecture-decision.
In an autonomous or headless run take only a policy-compliant non-Reserved path, never make a Reserved decision silently, and list unresolved Decision Requests in the final report.
Do not commit, push, merge, rebase, reset, force-push, delete branches or run any other repository-changing Git operation unless explicitly requested.
Parallel implementation work uses separate branches or worktrees; unrelated changes stay out of the current branch.

Run the matching workflow, which owns procedure, stop conditions and output (development-workflow for non-trivial changes, verify before completion, code-review/code-reviewer for reviews, build-fix, project-structure, add-dependency, custom-settings, architecture-decision, git-workflow, security-scan, delivery-pipeline).
Shared build configuration targets net10.0 for every .NET project below the root.
Shared build configuration enables Nullable reference types, ImplicitUsings and AnalysisLevel latest for every .NET project below the root.
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-023 places shared settings but no oracle policy chooses nullable reference types, implicit usings or the latest analyzer level; the template makes them effective defaults.

normative_action: Every register entry is Decided; changing an entry is Reserved and runs architecture-decision; policy detail stays with the Details-in owner.

D-01 Clean Architecture: Domain, Application, Infrastructure, Api production projects with inward dependencies; Controllers are the HTTP entry point; Application Services orchestrate use cases; specific repositories with IUnitOfWork as the commit boundary; simple Domain entities.
D-02 not adopted: CQRS handlers, MediatR, Kommand, VSA or similar mediator-based organization; introducing any of them requires explicit approval.
D-03 backend platform: .NET 10 LTS on its latest stable servicing release, C# 14, ASP.NET Core, Controllers; moving to a preview/RC .NET or C# release requires approval.
D-04 persistence: EF Core with Microsoft SQL Server (Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer); provider concerns stay out of Application and Domain.
D-05 validation: FluentValidation for explicit request and use-case validation.
D-06 logging: ILogger<T> in application code with Serilog as provider (Serilog.AspNetCore; sinks only as required).

D-07 Swashbuckle Swagger UI (Swashbuckle.AspNetCore) is the Development interactive documentation and manual-testing surface at /swagger, exposed outside Development only when requirements justify it.

D-08 backend tests: NUnit; test projects under backend/ beside production projects; WebApplicationFactory<Program> (Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing) for integration tests; Testcontainers conditional.
D-09 frontend: current stable Angular via the CLI (CLI-selected TypeScript/RxJS), standalone APIs, strict mode, routing, zoneless when supported, SCSS, Angular Material/CDK, Vitest; npm workspace.
D-10 not added by default: NgRx, Axios, Lodash, Bootstrap, Tailwind or additional form/component/state libraries; built-in Angular capabilities first, extras need a concrete requirement.
D-11 mapping: manual mapping for simple cases; Mapster (Mapster, Mapster.DependencyInjection) when mapping volume warrants it.
D-12 resilience: Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience for HttpClient and Microsoft.Extensions.Resilience for other pipelines, approved only when a real integration needs resilience.
D-13 frontend E2E: Playwright is the approved default when E2E coverage is required, not part of the minimal scaffold.
D-15 API versioning is not adopted until a published-compatibility need exists; when adopted, Asp.Versioning with its Controller integration.
D-16 solution format .slnx; legacy .sln only when an external tool or requirement needs it.
D-17 repository-level Directory.Build.props for genuinely shared settings and Directory.Packages.props for Central Package Management; project-specific settings stay in their projects.
D-18 layout: backend/<Name>.<Layer>/ for production and backend test projects, frontend/<Name>.Web/ for the Angular workspace, docs/ for documentation; no separate top-level tests/ directory.
